claims.text: A controlled heat treatment can induce a 5–10 vol.% fraction of uniformly distributed coherent nanoprecipitates in a W-based refractory high-entropy alloy such as WTaCrVHf.
Introducing the coherent nanoprecipitates will enhance the radiation tolerance of the W-based refractory high-entropy alloy.
Introducing the coherent nanoprecipitates will preserve the mechanical integrity of the alloy.
Annealing at 800–1000 °C is a sub-solvus treatment for the proposed W-based refractory high-entropy alloy.
A stepwise 800–1000 °C annealing treatment under inert atmosphere can nucleate and grow coherent nanoprecipitates in the alloy.
Controlled heat-treatment times can produce a uniform nanoprecipitate dispersion while avoiding precipitate coarsening.
The nanoprecipitates will remain stable at the proposed irradiation temperatures.
Coherent nanoprecipitates act as sinks for irradiation-induced point defects.
Defect absorption at the nanoprecipitates promotes point-defect recombination.
Enhanced point-defect recombination reduces the accumulation of harmful irradiation-induced defect clusters and voids.
Coherent precipitate–matrix interfaces permit efficient dislocation transmission.
Efficient dislocation transmission across coherent interfaces maintains yield strength and ductility.
After reactor-relevant irradiation, the heat-treated alloy will have more than 30% lower defect-cluster and void density than the untreated baseline.
After irradiation, the heat-treated alloy's yield strength will remain comparable to that of the original alloy.
After irradiation, the heat-treated alloy's ductility will remain comparable to that of the original alloy.
The radiation-tolerance benefit may diminish if irradiation temperatures cause precipitate coarsening.
The radiation-tolerance benefit may diminish if the precipitate volume fraction falls significantly outside the 5–10% target range.
Studies in related alloys support a beneficial role for coherent nanoprecipitates in radiation tolerance.
